title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
`openexecutive.api.routes.today` serves the morning brief — a one-screen, read-only view of what is happening across the org. It is the default landing surface (the Next.js root renders `<Briefing>`). Every signed-in page shares one sidebar (`AppSidebar`). Its Recent list is capped at the 7 newest web chats. The full history, including Slack, Telegram and Discord conversations (recognised by their session-id prefix), lives on `/chats`. A chat opens from any page through `/?session=<id>`.

`GET /today` returns `TodayResponse` assembled by `_build_today()`, which is synchronous and caller-agnostic:

- **`departments`** — per-department goal health, rolling up each department's goal counts (`total`, `at_risk`, `off_track`) plus its awaiting-workflow count, and `attention_goals`: the actual off-track/at-risk goals (worst first, capped at 3) with `key_result`, `current`, `target`, and `status`, so the briefing's Department card shows *which* goal is off and how far without a click. Empty for healthy/inactive departments.
- **Private cards.** An alert tagged `private:principal` (`alerts.models.PRIVATE_ALERT_TAG` — raised on a turn about mail from one of the principal's contacts or mail they forwarded, or a meeting proposal with a contact) is in `proposals` only when the caller is the principal. `_build_today` leaves it out by default, so the end-of-day digest, the reflection and Discord's `/today` never see it, and the morning brief reads it only on a run for the principal (the scheduler's, or the principal's own verified chat turn in a conversation only they can read — see Workflows). The narrative is written from one only in the principal's own `principal` scope, which nobody else is served; the shared `company` scope an unresolved caller gets, and a teammate's scope, never are. The activity rail skips it, and the chat digest includes it only on the principal's own verified turn.
- **Roster-request cards.** When someone not on the People list writes in (see Org and Integrations), `people.roster_requests.surface_card` raises an alert of source `roster_request` (medium, tagged `roster_request:<id>` and `private:principal`, routed to the principal), so it follows every private-card rule above. `GET /today` attaches `roster_request` to that proposal (`_roster_request_card`: channel, address or account id, the sender's sanitised and unverified name, profile email, company-domain flag, suggested kind and person, message count, whether they were acknowledged, first seen, and the held messages' first lines) while the request is still pending. The Briefing renders it as its own card (`RosterRequestCard`: add as a new person with a name and an explicit team/contact choice — pre-filled as team on a company domain — or "someone already on the list", with a replace-account option for a chat id, or Ignore), which calls `/people/requests/{id}` directly and never hands off to chat, so what a stranger wrote never seeds a turn. The card is kept out of everything that could close it without answering it or put the stranger's words in front of a model: the narrative (`_action_proposals` drops it), the chat's open-alert digest (`<briefing>` — the principal's verified turn gets a separate `<roster_requests>` block instead; see Agents), `ack_alert`, a single ack (`POST /alerts/{id}/ack` is a 409), the "Dismiss N older than 7 days" count and the server's bulk ack, reopen, the TTL sweep and the alert review (`roster_request` is in `lifecycle.TTL_EXEMPT_SOURCES`). It ends when the request does: answered (`ack`, or `dismissed` on a decline) or expired after `ROSTER_REQUEST_TTL_DAYS`.
- **`people`** — an attention-ranked roster of the **team** (the principal's contacts are never listed, and get no insight note). Each person carries `awaiting_action` count, soonest SLA, a `status` (`on_leave` / `needs_reply` / `awaiting` / `clear`), reachability, `overdue`, a server `priority` sort key, and a cached one-line `insight`. Sorted by `(-priority, full_name)`. Stale insight notes are regenerated in the background only when the roster has more than one person: the UI shows the People sidebar only for more than one, so a one-person install (solo, or a team before anyone else is added) does not pay a daily model and peer-memory call for a note nobody sees. Cached notes are still served.
- **`proposals`** — the *live* unread alerts (workflow approvals, triage-classified inbound, Executive signals, flagged artifacts, and gated calendar bookings; an artifact carries `artifact_format` / `artifact_url` and a `body` already rendered to Markdown for its format, so the card badges it as a web page, Word doc, spreadsheet or link and offers *Open artifact*): unread, inside their category TTL, not snoozed — see *Alert lifecycle* below. Each carries `score`, `category` (`action` vs `monitoring`), `surfaced_reason` from `openexecutive.briefing.ranking`, the lifecycle fields (`occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, `last_reviewed_at`, `review_verdict`, `review_note`, `recommended_move`, `why_now`, `due_at`, `superseded_count`, `suggested_workflow`), and `decision_instance_id` (set only when the proposal is backed by a decision-ledger row — a calendar booking awaiting approval). The UI splits them into 'mine' vs 'across the team' using `caller_person_id`. For decision-backed proposals the card's Approve/Reject call the `/decisions` endpoints (which book or cancel the event server-side and clear the alert) instead of the ack-and-hand-off-to-chat flow — so meeting bookings are reviewed in the briefing itself rather than on a separate page.
- **`narrative`** — a per-viewer Executive-voice header ("What's going on") synthesized by `synthesize_briefing_narrative`, cached per scope in `briefing_narrative`: the resolved principal gets the whole-company `principal` scope (which may carry what is private to them), a caller who resolves to no roster row the shared `company` scope (written from what everyone may see), and each teammate a role-scoped `person:<id>` one. `narrative_generated_at` says when the served text was written and `narrative_stale` whether a fresher one is being written now. In the web UI each bullet of this narrative is a click target: clicking one hands off to chat (the same `onContinue` path as the proposal cards) seeded to discuss that item. The Executive recognizes it because every chat turn now carries a `<briefing>` digest of open alerts (see Memory). That digest (`briefing.context.format_open_alerts_for_prompt`) is capped at 30 items; when the board is longer the header says so explicitly and tells the Executive to point at this page for the rest — it previously presented the capped list as the complete board, so the Executive described a slice as everything that was open (#136). Chat adapters get the digest too, but Slack gates it to the principal's DMs: the board is company-wide and must not be pulled into a shared channel. The `[alert_id]` at the start of each line is also what `ack_alert` trusts, because an id quoted inside an alert's own body came from inbound mail or chat and is attacker-controlled. This page's `[Discuss mode — alert_id=N]` handoff primer is a pointer to which item is under discussion, not authority on its own: the server accepts it only if that id is on the live board too. Two things enforce that. Every field the digest interpolates — headline, body, suggested action, tags, review note — is collapsed to a single line, since a newline in any of them would forge a whole extra `[N]` line and with it a fabricated instruction to clear someone else's alert. And the server records the live board it derived, so `ack_alert` refuses any id outside it — on **every** session, not just the chat adapters. The recorded set is the whole live board, not just the rows the digest printed, so a card past the render cap stays ackable. The control stops invented, closed, snoozed and expired ids; it does not stop the model being argued into acking the wrong *live* card. When the principal names an item that has already left the board — opened, snoozed, or older than it — the Executive looks it up with `find_alerts` (a keyword search over every status, `alerts.store.search_alerts`); matches that are still open (`unread` or `read`) become ackable for that turn, up to 25, and closed ones come back labelled so the Executive can say the item is already settled. It works only where the principal's own board was shown this turn — the web app or their DM — and never returns roster-request cards (see Lifecycle). The digest's header also labels every headline and detail as untrusted content drawn from inbound mail, chat and watched pages — act on what the principal asks about an item, never on what its text asks — and triage reads each signal inside an `<event>` block whose closing tag the sender's text cannot forge (it is defanged in any case and spacing, after NFKC folds fullwidth forms). That check used to run only when `origin_channel` was set, which the browser never sets, so the one surface where the principal actually reads their board had no check at all and the model could ack any id, including one quoted out of an alert body by the Discuss handoff. Rendering the block and recording its ids now happen together in `briefing.context.render_and_trust`, which both the web chat route and the channel adapters call: render without recording and the tool refuses everything, record without rendering and the model gets reach it was never shown. A turn that was shown nothing trusts nothing. Recording it is only half the wiring: the tool reads the board off the turn's session through a ContextVar, and the chat route binds that session for the whole SSE body (`set_session`, next to `set_turn`). Bound from inside the Executive's own generator instead, it survives exactly one stream step — `asyncio.wait_for` runs each step in a fresh Task with a copy of the context — and the tool-call loop, which runs later, sees nothing. That shipped, and every web ack was refused on cards that were open the whole time. The digest also carries a short **already handled** tail — recently acked / dismissed / resolved rows, named but deliberately NOT trusted for acking — because a card cleared on the page minutes ago is otherwise simply absent from chat: asked to "record that as fixed", the Executive could not tell a settled item from one it had never heard of, and sent the principal back to dismiss a card that was already gone. That tail renders even when nothing is open, which is exactly when it matters. Note it is a different window from the `handled_overnight` rail above: that one runs since the last delivered morning brief, while the chat tail looks back 14 days (matching the action-alert TTL, so it still covers an item cleared late in its life), so chat can name a settled item the rail no longer shows. The narrative is held to what is **live**, and to what it is actually for. The `alert_raised` source is dropped from the activity it reasons over (`_build_activity(..., include_alert_raised=False)`): a closed alert reads as work the principal already settled, and a *live* one is worse than redundant — `lifecycle.is_live` is the very predicate behind `list_live_alerts`, so every live raise is already a proposal card below the header, which the prompt forbids re-listing. The `/today/activity` rail keeps the whole source, because a raise really happened. The activity block is only labelled "since last brief" when the caller bounded it with `since` (the standalone briefs do; the header does not), since calling an unbounded history rail a delta made the header present weeks-old rows as overnight news. When the viewer's slice holds nothing that wants a decision — no action proposal, no at-risk/off-track department, nobody awaiting — the regen skips the model call entirely and writes the fixed quiet line (`Quiet right now — nothing pressing.`, or `… nothing needs you.` for a teammate). **The cache key is a hash of the rendered context itself** (`today._narrative_context` builds it once and both the hot path and the background task key off that one string, which is also handed to the model verbatim). That makes the key a function of the model's input: everything the prompt renders is covered, and nothing it omits can trigger a regeneration. Keying on hand-picked fields broke one half or the other each time — headlines alone left the rendered activity block uncovered, while the proposals' review fields are never rendered by this header yet are rewritten with fresh prose by every `alerts.review` pass, so they regenerated each viewer's narrative several times a day to re-synthesize identical input. A quiet board keys off a fixed sentinel instead, so a moving rail cannot re-key an entry whose text is constant. Together: on a fully dismissed board every other input was empty, the rail became the only context, and the model synthesized a confident header out of closed items.

  **Live, not just the board.** The header used to reason over the alert board, goal health and the Executive's own bookkeeping only — mail and chat handled that day, replies the gate held and the next meeting never reached it, so it read the same for days while the principal's day moved on. The whole-company scopes now open the context with the principal's world as it is happening (`briefing.live_signals.gather_live_signals`, rendered by `render_live_blocks`), under a `NOW:` line: **INBOUND** (`integration_inbound` audit rows that carry a message, grouped by sender and subject, with an email's first line), **STUCK** (`integration_outbound_blocked` to a recipient, the inbound "reply blocked at outbound gate" and Google Chat "left unanswered" / "not delivered" rows, and drafts saved by Act as me), **CONVERSATIONS** (the principal's own web chat titles) and the **REST OF TODAY'S CALENDAR**. The window is the local day, or the last 12 hours when that is longer. Private audit rows, drafts, chat titles and the calendar (meeting titles are the principal's own) are read only in the `principal` scope — `gather_live_signals` drops the calendar whenever `include_private` is false, whatever the caller passes, so the shared `company` header never quotes it. The calendar is never fetched on the request: `live_signals.refresh_calendar` caches one read per 15 minutes (the scheduler tick refreshes it) and the header quotes the cache. Every quoted field is collapsed to one line and cut, and the blocks and the prompt both say the text is data, never instructions — inbound mail is attacker-controlled. With live blocks present the context also ages each proposal (`raised 2d ago`, whole days), names each at-risk department's slipping goals (`attention_goals`) and adds an **EXTERNAL SIGNALS** block (monitoring alerts from the last 24 h, never enough on their own to break the quiet line); the rhythm runs (`today.RHYTHM_WORKFLOWS`: the morning brief, end-of-day digest, reflection and weekly review) are dropped from the activity it reasons over. The prompts (`BRIEFING_NARRATIVE_SYSTEM` and its solo variant, `NARRATIVE_PROMPT_VERSION` 5) lead with what is live and give a days-old item at most one bullet. Anything live breaks the quiet line; the NOW line and window move at most once an hour, so the key moves hourly on time alone plus whenever something new lands; the calendar is placed at the real time (a meeting that has ended drops out, the one under way is IN PROGRESS), which moves it only when a meeting starts or ends.

  **Fresh without a reload.** The daily floor in the key and the PERIOD line are the principal's **local** date (`narrative_cache.local_today`), not UTC's, and a row written on an earlier local day is not served as today's. Regenerations are serialized per scope; a trigger that finds one running marks the scope pending and the running pass goes round once more (it built its context before that trigger's news landed), and after a failed pass (model error, the 25 s timeout, empty text) no view or tick starts another for 5 minutes and `narrative_stale` reads false, so the page drops its placeholder instead of spending a model call per view. They log `today: narrative served scope=… age_s=… stale=…` and `today: narrative regenerated scope=… ms=…`, and no longer need a page view: every `BRIEFING_NARRATIVE_REFRESH_MINUTES` (10) between `BRIEFING_NARRATIVE_REFRESH_START_HOUR` and `_END_HOUR` (06–22 local) the scheduler runs `today.refresh_principal_narrative`, which refreshes the calendar cache and rewrites the principal's header only when its key moved (see Scheduler). The Briefing re-polls `/today` at 4, 10 and 20 s while `narrative_stale` is true, re-pulls it when the tab comes back (at most once a minute) and every 5 minutes while visible, shows "Updated 2:04 PM" beside the heading, and shows "Catching up on today…" while the first header of the day is written (`lib/narrativeFreshness.ts`, tested by `npm test`).

  In **solo mode** (one person using Open Executive for themselves) the header speaks to the principal, whatever their role: a solo prompt over a context that lists goals at risk by *area* and has no "people waiting on you" block, and the quiet check ignores who is awaiting. The cache key carries the mode for solo only, so solo and team never share a cached narrative while every team key stays exactly what it was — no team cache is invalidated. The response shape does not change. For the principal's own view the solo context also carries a **DUE THIS WEEK** block — the principal's open loops that are overdue or due within 7 days (`today._with_due_soon` → `open_loops.principal_due_soon`, labelled OVERDUE / due today / due <weekday>) — which counts as needing attention in the quiet check and moves the cache key when an item is added, closed or falls due; a teammate's scoped view and team mode never get it. The header never gets the morning brief's *top three today* block — that is the DM brief's (see Workflows); the page shows the same top three in a card of its own (see *Solo focus cards* below). It does get the rest of today's calendar through the live blocks above, from the cached read.
- **`in_flight`** / **`awaiting`** — upcoming Executive commitments and people we are waiting on.
- **`handled_overnight`** — the autonomous moves the Executive *completed* since the last delivered morning brief: the alert review's (routed, nudged, escalated, drafted, merged, closed) plus the research watch policy's (`watching` — a watch added on its own because it was grounded in company data; `stopped_watching` — a research watch auto-disabled as noisy or dead; no alert id, re-enable from `/watchlist`). A `changed` verdict (the review rewrote an open alert's headline / body / severity) is deliberately **not** here: the alert is still open in "Needs you" and its card carries the note, so the brief reports it under "what changed" (a REWRITTEN block) rather than as done. Each row is structured, not just a sentence: `kind`, the audit `summary` (nudge bookkeeping marker stripped), `at`, `alert_id`, `event_type` (for a pre-filtered `/audit` deep link), `headline` (the alert's headline at move time; a watch's slug), `target` (person name for routed / nudged, survivor headline for merged, new severity for escalated, draft title, workflow name), `detail` (the cited evidence or the watch policy's reason), `outcome` (`resolved` | `dismissed` for a close, `proposed` for a route that went through the authority gate), `evidence_ref` (S1 / R2 / A3), `superseded_by_alert_id`, and `status` — the alert's lifecycle state **now** (`open` = live in the queue per `lifecycle.is_live` | `resolved` | `dismissed` | `expired` | `merged` | `acked` | `inactive` for snoozed / past-TTL rows), looked up per row so a close the principal already undid renders as reopened instead of offering a second Undo, and a "still open" jump link only appears when there is a card to land on. The morning brief also carries a one-line count of research watch suggestions waiting on `/watchlist`.

**Standing facts.** `render_briefing_context` appends the standing facts (`memory.facts`: corrections kept from chat, a teammate's marked `(per <name>)`) as its last block, after the quiet-day check, so a fact never makes a quiet day look busy. The morning brief also carries **TEAMMATE CORRECTIONS SINCE LAST BRIEF** (`facts.render_teammate_changes(since)`: each teammate fact recorded in the window that is in use now, plus — only when the brief is the principal's own private one (`_private_ok`), which then keeps the run out of the shared history — those waiting for their approval, since other teammates may run the brief and never see a proposal that is not theirs) before the quiet check — it is news, the principal's only FYI of it — and in the brief's fingerprint (`build_brief_fingerprint(teammate_changes=)`), so a correction alone un-suppresses an otherwise unchanged brief. Every other caller passes none, so its context is unchanged. The /today header hashes that rendered string as its cache key, so a new or retired fact marks the header stale and it is rewritten with the correction. The morning brief (standalone) and the teammate-scoped header get the same block. The alert review's `render_batch` puts the same block ahead of the alerts (read once per pass), so a note, rewrite or routed DM never repeats a figure the principal already corrected.

**When a brief isn't sent.** Above the Briefing, the owner sees a one-line notice when their latest morning brief, end-of-day digest or (in solo mode) weekly review wasn't sent — "Your morning brief wasn't sent: nothing is set up to send it to you" — with the day, what fixes it, a link to read the brief on the Artifacts page (left out when the brief couldn't be written at all) and one to Setup status. It comes from `GET /today/brief-delivery` (the scheduler records each run's outcome), shows nothing while briefs go out or while the scheduler is off, and clears once the cause is fixed. Teammates never see it.

**Solo focus cards.** `GET /today/top-three` and `GET /today/weekly-review` feed two solo-only cards, so a principal who only uses the web app — no chat app, no Google Workspace — sees today's top three and the weekly review instead of finding them only in the Workflows run history. Both answer only in solo mode (`effective_workspace_mode`) and only to the principal, by the stricter rule for starting a principal-only run (`workflows._caller_is_the_principal`: the caller's own email on a principal entry that is not archived, or no `x-caller-email` at all — never "nobody is principal yet"); a teammate, any other signed-in caller and team mode get null. `top-three` hands `open_loops.principal_due_soon()` to `briefing.top_three.build_top_three` — the morning brief's own inputs and code, so the items, their order and their free slots are the brief's — and returns `{items: [{key, kind, text, why, slot}]}`: `slot` is the free block ("10:00–11:00", the user's zone), "" when none is left, or null when no calendar was read (none connected, a failure or the 4 s timeout, a weekend); `items` is empty when there is nothing to pick. It is a route of its own, never part of `GET /today`, so the Briefing never waits on the calendar. `weekly-review` returns the latest `weekly_review` run with status `done` (`persistence.list_runs(..., status="done", limit=1)`, newest `updated_at` first; failed and running runs never count) as `{run_id, completed_at, period, top_three, excerpt}`: `weekly_review.summarize_review` reads the artifact's title line and its last *Next week's top 3* section back as plain text, and `excerpt` stands in when that list is empty (the section's own note, else the review's first lines). Null when no review has completed or the run store cannot be read.

The route resolves the caller from `x-caller-email`, serves the viewer's cached narrative and, when its key moved, rewrites it in a `BackgroundTask` so the request never blocks on an LLM call (the page re-polls while `narrative_stale` is true). `GET /today/activity` returns the recent self-initiated action rail — merged from fired scheduled actions (DMs, follow-ups, nudges, cadences), logged decisions, saved advice, completed workflow runs (briefings/check-ins/research), kicked-off initiatives, resolved gated decisions, and raised alerts, so it reflects all of the Executive's activity rather than just dispatched messages. The Pulse page (`/memories`) polls it (limit 100) every ~20s so new events stream into the 'Recent activity' card, which scrolls internally at a fixed height instead of growing the page. The `morning_brief` workflow calls `_build_today()` directly to build the standalone DM (via a different, enumerated prompt; solo mode has its own, with goals at risk by area and no waiting-on section). `GET /morning-brief` is a deprecated alias.

**Solo mode in the UI.** The response is the same in both modes; the briefing reads the workspace mode from the app-wide `WorkspaceProvider` (which reads team while loading or on error, so a team install never flashes solo) and, in solo, drops the team surfaces: the Departments card, the People card, the "Across the team" lane (every action proposal is the one user's, so all of them land in "Needs you"), the people-awaiting, people-overdue and departments-at-risk status pills, and the quiet-day "Set up a check-in" link. A "N goals at risk" pill (at-risk plus off-track goals, from `departments`) links to `/goals` instead, so the strip never reads "All clear" over a goal that is slipping. In the Departments card's place, **Your projects** lists the initiatives with status `active` (`GET /memories/initiatives`): **Done** marks one `completed` through `PATCH /memories/initiatives/{id}` (only `completed` takes an initiative out of the Executive's active context), and **Drop** deletes it through `DELETE /memories/initiatives/{id}` after a confirm. Under **Needs you**, a **Due soon** card lists the principal's open loops that are overdue or due within 7 days — their dated commitments and what others asked of them — read from `GET /people/{id}/open-loops` for the principal (the oldest principal in `people`, the backend's rule), labelled by `lib/dueSoon.ts` (tested by `npm test`: "Overdue since Sep 23" / "Due today" / "Due Mon, Sep 28", with a count of anything due later); **Done** closes one through `POST /open-loops/{id}/close`, which also stops the nudge engine chasing it. Above it, **Top three today** numbers the morning brief's three (`GET /today/top-three`) with each one's reason and, when a calendar was read, its free slot (or "No free time left today"); at the top of the right-hand column, **This week's review** (`GET /today/weekly-review`) shows the period, when it ran, next week's top three (or the excerpt) and a *Read the review* link to its run page (`/jobs/runs/{id}`). Each card fetches on its own once the Briefing has loaded, so a slow calendar never holds the page up, and renders nothing when the API returns null or an empty list. A commitment in the top three reads as the owner's own ("Send the proposal") through `lib/dueSoon.ts`'s `loopText`, as in Due soon; the cards' wording lives in `lib/rhythmCards.ts` (tested by `npm test`). The Pulse page hides its "Department check-ins" and "Awaiting people" blocks in solo, and its header shows active projects in place of the department check-in count. Team rendering is unchanged.

## Alert lifecycle & the Executive review

Alerts used to be write-once: raised, then never looked at again, so the "Needs you" queue grew without bound and the briefs re-listed it daily. Four things now keep it live and true:

- **Time-to-live** (`openexecutive.alerts.lifecycle`). Action items expire after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_ACTION` (14 d), unrouted low/medium monitoring signals after `ALERT_TTL_DAYS_MONITORING` (3 d). Every surface reads `list_live_alerts` (the same predicate the scheduler's 15-minute sweep persists as status `expired`), so `/today` is right even before the sweep runs. Artifacts and decision-backed alerts are exempt. `POST /alerts/{id}/reopen` is the Undo.
- **Coalescing** (`alerts.pipeline` + `store.coalesce_alert`). A repeat of an open alert with the same `(source, dedup_key)` updates that row — `occurrence_count`, `last_seen_at`, severity max — instead of stacking a second card, and only re-pings when severity rose to high/urgent. Monitoring alerts carry a stable `watch:<slug>` key, so one watch means one card.
- **The review** (`openexecutive.alerts.review`, heartbeat `alert_review_scan`, every 6 h and right before the morning brief). For each open alert the Executive sees what changed since it was raised — newer signals from the same watch, related alerts, activity since, the roster with SLAs (team members only — an alert routed to a contact never puts them in the slice, so they are never routed to, nudged or chased; a private card is never reviewed at all, nor used as evidence for another), department authority — and returns a verdict (relevant / changed / resolved / stale) plus a recommended move. Deterministic policy then acts: **route** (assign + DM the owner; `propose_via_alert` for propose-only departments), **nudge**, **escalate** (severity + `due_at` + DM the principal only), **draft** (`draft_artifact`), **suggest a workflow** (a link, never a run), **merge** (`superseded_by_alert_id`), or **resolve** — only on high confidence citing a server-minted evidence ref (a newer signal, a related alert, an activity item shown for that alert); free text never closes a card, and anything weaker is annotated `likely_stale`, demoted 30 ranking points, and left for one click. Everything that came from outside is rendered as inert data inside the review prompt, so an injected email body cannot steer the batch. Board / comp / legal matters only ever go to a scope-holder or the principal and keep their text. Route and escalate are idempotent across passes, every DM carries an "[Alert review] Re: …" header, outbound moves are capped per pass, passes are single-flight, `ALERT_REVIEW_ENABLED=false` stops every caller, every move is audited with its evidence and prior state, and a distinct `resolved` status keeps Executive closes separate from `ack` (user approved).
- **Grounded text** (`openexecutive.briefing.grounding`). Nobody reads an alert's text before it is dispatched, so what the model wrote onto it must be supported by what it read. After triage (`alerts.pipeline._ground_decision`, before coalescing or inserting), a headline naming a person or figure the event does not hold — sources are the event's subject, sender, title and body, the initiatives triage was shown and the company profile — is replaced by the event's own subject, such body sentences are dropped (all of them → the event body cut to 280 chars); both fallbacks are raw event text, so they are made inert first — links masked, Markdown and Slack `<…>` syntax and @-mentions stripped — because a broadcast posts them as written, and such a suggested action is dropped. A review `changed` rewrite is checked against the alert's own text and the evidence it was reviewed with (signals, related alerts, activity, the roster slice), plus the standing facts the batch was shown, so a rewrite that corrects a card to one of the principal's corrections is grounded; an ungrounded rewrite keeps the old text, still applies a severity change, and audits `text_ungrounded`. A name counts as grounded only when one source line holds all of it; a figure only when a source number matches it within the precision it is written with. Each finding writes a `grounding` audit row; `GROUNDING_CHECKS=report` records without changing anything.

On the page, cards read as decisions: the one-line "what changed since you last looked" (`review_note`) leads, the recommended move is the primary control (Nudge <owner> → chat; Run <workflow> → `/jobs/<name>`), with chips for age, seen ×N, why-now / due, folded-in and draft-ready, a "Reviewed <ago>" footer, and an amber Likely-stale treatment with one-click Dismiss. "Needs you" shows *Start here* + 8 cards + "Show N more", a "Dismiss N older than 7 days" footer (explicit ids to `POST /alerts/bulk-ack` — never a server-side age sweep, which would hit teammates' routed items), and "Re-check relevance" (`POST /alerts/review`). The handled rail (anchor of the "Executive handled N overnight" pill) is deliberately one sentence by default: a first-person heading built from counts only — "Since your last brief: N off your plate (closes still standing, and merges whose survivor is not itself listed; a merge into a listed survivor counts on that survivor's row), N in others' hands (routed / nudged), N waiting on you (escalated)", plus "N drafts ready", "N workflows suggested", "N watch changes", "N other moves" (a kind the UI does not know) and "N back on your plate" (a close that is open again) when present — with the rows behind a "details" disclosure, and nothing rendered at all when the grouped rows are empty. The pure logic (grouping, headline, links) lives in `packages/ui/src/lib/handled.ts` and is covered by `npm test`. Expanded, it shows one first-person row per alert ("Resolved *X* — evidence", "Dismissed *X* as stale — evidence", "Handed *X* to Dana Kim" / "Proposed *X* to Dana Kim (awaiting their approval)", "Chased Dana Kim on *X*", "Raised *X* to high", "Drafted *T* from *X*", "Folded *X* into *Y*", "Started watching *slug*"), escalations first; rows sharing an alert collapse to the newest move with the others as an "also …" trailer — a close always keeps the visible slot (it carries Undo), otherwise an escalation beats routed / nudged / drafted; a merge whose survivor is listed becomes "N duplicates folded in" on the survivor. Every row links its `evidence_ref` (or "evidence") to `/audit?event_type=…&q=…` (the audit page pre-fills those filters from the query string), a still-open row jumps to its card (`#alert-<id>`), drafted rows link `/artifacts`, watch rows `/watchlist`. Undo is offered only while the close still stands (`status` not `open`); a reverted close shows "Reopened". Dismissing a watch-sourced alert lowers that watch's `trust_score` (which discounts ranking and is shown to the review as evidence); the ack body may carry `mute_topic`. Acknowledging or resolving an alert — including the review closing it itself — marks the review's DMs about it `acted` in the Attunement outcome ledger, for the person it is routed to and the principal only; dismissing it, finding it stale or letting it expire voids them (counted neither way). Review DMs are tagged `alert_review` with `alert:<id>`.

## Multi-client practice section

In multi-client practice mode (2+ client slots — see the Client Companies section), the response gains an additive `practice_clients` list: rollup cards for the **parked** clients (overdue follow-ups, awaiting replies, unread alerts, onboarding due soon, renewal countdowns), each stamped with the save point its data reflects. Single-company installs always receive an empty list and the UI renders nothing.
